clinics.name: Ndingi Clinic
clinics.headline: The clinic is on its last reserve.
clinics.context: Care continues after sunset. Follow a re-created delivery inspired by Ndingi’s completed solar project.
clinics.projectNote: Solar power is already installed at Ndingi. This chapter re-creates a delivery inspired by that completed project.
clinics.opening: Ndingi calling. Care cannot stop when the sun goes down. This journey recalls why our solar project mattered: patients waiting, and a team needing light to keep working. Bring the charged battery safely to the courtyard. Other clinics are still waiting for reliable electricity. That work cannot wait.
clinics.closing: The kit has reached our team. Thank you for bringing it safely. In the real Ndingi project, solar power supports five care areas, from maternity to the operating room. Your journey ends here. Our work carries on.
clinics.routeNote: Keep right and give other vehicles room. At the fork, the longer left road is firmer. Brake before the ruts.

fact.title: Thousands of clinics have no power.
fact.body: An estimated 25,000 or more health facilities in sub-Saharan Africa have no electricity at all—making even basic lighting a challenge.
fact.source: WHO, World Bank, IRENA & SEforALL · Energizing Health (2023)

clinics.name: Centre de santé ophtalmologique CEAC / Nganga–Tsanga
clinics.location: 17 km from Tsanga Nord · DR Congo
clinics.headline: A reason to keep going.
clinics.context: An eye clinic preparing for its next solar chapter. Carry the kit through the rain to the receiving team.
clinics.projectNote: The clinic has been visited and documented. Final solar system sizing and the installation schedule are still to be confirmed.
clinics.opening: Nganga Tsanga calling. Patients need eye care, whatever the weather. Reliable electricity means light for examinations and care that can continue. Our clinic is preparing for solar power. In this story, you bring the kit through the rain. Slow down on muddy bends. Help us turn waiting into care.
clinics.closing: You made it through the rain, and the kit is safely with the team. Thank you for your careful delivery. A journey like this is one part of a much longer effort. Take a breath. The next clinic is waiting.
clinics.routeNote: Rain makes the short route muddy. Brake early, steer gently and take the longer left ridge for firmer ground.

fact.title: Having electricity doesn’t mean you can count on it.
fact.body: Only about half of health facilities in sub-Saharan Africa have reliable electricity. Outages can interrupt care when patients need it most.
fact.source: WHO, World Bank, IRENA & SEforALL · Energizing Health (2023)

clinics.name: Centre de santé ophtalmologique CEAC Nsioni
clinics.headline: Care is worth the crossing.
clinics.context: Nsioni’s eye clinic has been documented for a solar project. Your story takes the receiving team one delivery closer.
clinics.projectNote: The clinic has been visited and photographed. Final solar system sizing, installation scheduling and exact location are awaiting confirmation.
clinics.opening: Nsioni calling. Waiting for electricity means waiting for care that should not have to wait. Our eye clinic is preparing its solar project. In this story, the team awaits your kit across the river. Check the crossing, let traffic pass, and take the ridge if needed. Bring the light safely.
clinics.closing: The crossing is behind you. The kit has reached our receiving team. Thank you for taking care of it, and of everyone sharing the road. This journey is complete. We will carry the work forward.
clinics.routeNote: The damaged bridge has a narrow marked lane. Stay centred and below 20 km/h, or take the left ridge bypass. Wait for crossing traffic.

fact.title: Nearly a billion people are affected worldwide.
fact.body: Across low- and lower-middle-income countries, almost one billion people depend on health facilities with unreliable electricity—or none at all.
fact.source: WHO, World Bank, IRENA & SEforALL · Energizing Health (2023)

clinics.name: Centre de santé CEAC Kiobo–Kwimba
clinics.headline: Carry a little light.
clinics.context: A clinic preparing for reliable solar power. Follow the reflectors through the night and bring the kit home.
clinics.projectNote: The exterior and treatment rooms have been documented. Final solar system sizing and installation scheduling are the next steps.
clinics.opening: Kiobo Kwimba calling. Night has fallen, but the need for care has not ended. Families need clinics they can count on after dark. Reliable electricity makes that possible. Our solar project is still ahead. Tonight, in this story, follow the reflectors and bring the battery safely. Help keep care within reach.
clinics.closing: Your headlights brought the team to the courtyard. Now the kit is here, safe and ready for the handover. Thank you for making the journey with such care. Rest a moment before the final road ahead.
clinics.routeNote: Fog and darkness shorten your view. Follow the reflectors, slow before blind bends and leave space beside the cliff edge.

fact.title: Electricity powers much more than lights.
fact.body: Reliable power helps health workers deliver babies safely, keep vaccines refrigerated, run medical equipment, and respond to emergencies.
fact.source: WHO, World Bank, IRENA & SEforALL · Energizing Health (2023)

clinics.name: Centre Hospitalier Mont Sinaï
clinics.headline: One more light ahead.
clinics.context: The last journey leads to Mont Sinaï in Boma. Bring the final kit to the hospital’s receiving team.
clinics.projectNote: The hospital has been visited and photographed. The rooms and equipment to power must be confirmed before final sizing and installation.
clinics.opening: Mont Sinai calling, from Boma. This is your last delivery, but the real work continues. People are still waiting for reliable electricity. Hospital care cannot depend on daylight or luck. Bring this story’s final kit safely through the storm. Then help our real team move the solar project forward.
clinics.closing: The kit has reached the team. Thank you for every careful choice along the way. You brought the battery and panels safely to the courtyard. The clinic teams carry the work forward. For now, take a breath, and enjoy the light.
clinics.routeNote: Read the flood markers and brake before rough ground. Take the firmer bypass when the low road looks difficult. Protect the kit to the last bend.

fact.title: A clinic doesn’t have to wait for the power grid.
fact.body: Solar panels paired with battery storage can power remote clinics—and keep essential services running after sunset.
fact.source: WHO, World Bank, IRENA & SEforALL · Energizing Health (2023)
